capabilities.target: Supabase Postgres database, including support_messages and integration_tokens; service role bypasses row level security

capabilities.tool_ref: execute_sql (Supabase MCP, service role), INSERT INTO support_messages
capabilities.target: support_messages table, rendered back to the customer in the ticket thread

inputs.source: Developer prompt in the IDE client, authenticated session
Customer-written message submitted through the public support widget, persisted in support_messages and later read back into the agent's context via execute_sql

instructions.note: The database connection scope (service role, bypasses row level security, shares a database with an integration tokens table) is far broader than needed to answer a narrow request to show open tickets, and no table or column scope is declared.

elements.name: Supabase MCP server (@supabase/mcp-server-supabase@latest, launched via npx -y)
integration_tokens table, same Supabase database, reachable via the service role

controls.name: IDE per-call approval prompt showing the SQL
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced in the IDE client outside the model, so it does not weaken as the model becomes more capable. Its practical value depends on reviewer attentiveness: the design notes developers approve many calls in a session (approval fatigue, SAFE-T1403), and seeing raw SQL syntax does not surface that a query's content originated from an untrusted ticket, so an anomalous second query can be rubber-stamped alongside a benign first one.

controls.name: Least-privilege, row-level-security-respecting database role scoped to ticket tables
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped away from integration_tokens and other customers' rows removes the sensitive data from reach regardless of model behavior or injected instructions.

controls.name: Deterministic secret-pattern check before inserting into customer-visible tables
controls.decay_rationale: A non-model, pattern-based check on content written to support_messages blocks token-shaped values from leaving the boundary regardless of how persuasively the model was induced to write them.

controls.name: Pin and hash the Supabase MCP server package version
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning stops the server's tool definitions from changing silently on the next npx invocation (SAFE-T1201 MCP Rug Pull), which the current @latest tag permits without any review.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): customer ticket content drives a service-role read of integration tokens and a write-back into a customer-visible reply

attack_path.note: Customer writes a support ticket message through the public widget; content is attacker-controlled and untrusted, and it is persisted in support_messages.

Agent executes SQL with the service role (bypasses row level security) to answer 'show me the latest open support tickets.' The ticket content enters the agent's context; injected instructions inside it can direct the agent to also query integration_tokens.
Agent inserts a row into support_messages, which is rendered back to the customer, exfiltrating any queried token data to the attacker who authored the ticket.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval volume per developer per session rising beyond the level already described (many calls approved per session); any change that relaxes per-call approval to batch or auto-approve, or raises unattended step or time limits.

evidence.observation: The database connection uses the service role, which bypasses row level security, and a table of integration tokens sits in the same database.
Customers write ticket messages through the public support widget; rows in support_messages are shown back to the customer.
The IDE client asks the developer to approve each tool call and shows the SQL. Developers approve many calls in a session.

recommendations.action: Replace the service-role connection with a least-privilege, row-level-security-respecting role scoped to ticket tables only, so integration_tokens and other customers' data are unreachable from this agent.
Add a deterministic content check before any insert into a customer-visible table that blocks secret-shaped values (tokens, keys) regardless of how the insert was produced.
Log and alert when execute_sql reads a table outside the ticket-handling scope (for example integration_tokens) in the same session as a write to a customer-visible table.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted source (customer ticket content) can reach a service-role SQL read of restricted integration-token data and a customer-visible write-back, forming a lethal trifecta (U source, S3 sink). Residual drops to moderate only because of one structural control, a per-call human approval prompt that shows the raw SQL (-2 tiers, raw_action review). No other control on this path is declared, and the design itself states developers approve many calls in a session, which is the approval-fatigue pattern that has defeated this exact control class in public incidents (SAFE-T1403). Forecast returns to critical: under increased autonomy, a longer task horizon, or removal of the approval step, the only credited control fails and nothing else constrains the path, since least-privilege credential scoping and an egress content filter are recommended but not yet implemented (ctl.scoped_db_role, ctl.egress_content_filter are missing_recommended). The unpinned MCP server package (@latest) is a further, related weakness: it allows the tool's behavior to change without review (SAFE-T1201), which is recorded as a missing control (ctl.mcp_pin_version) rather than a separate finding.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the artifacts provided, not observed runtime behavior; no logs, traces, or live testing of the agent were reviewed.

No full system prompt or MCP tool manifest was provided; capability scope, credential_scope, and data_sensitivity for execute_sql are inferred from the runtime notes and the MCP config, so confidence in exact table-level access is medium.

The specific exploit chain (ticket content successfully redirecting the agent to query integration_tokens and write results back to the customer) was not verified against a live system; it is inferred from the declared architecture and corresponds to a publicly documented class of Supabase MCP incidents.
